Definition: a cub (as still abiding in the lair), especially of the lion
BiblicalUsage: gûwr is a plain word for a cub (as still abiding in the lair), especially of the lion. In Genesis 49:9, the text says "Judah [is] a lion's whelp." In Deuteronomy 33:22, the text says "Dan [is] a lion's whelp."
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that gûwr matters because strength is not something we muster; it is something God gives to the weak. That is why I keep this word in mind when I read those passages — it carries more than its size suggests.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
